justification: Fixes five live-verified truth defects in the conveyancing PDF (a legal due-diligence document): a fabricated LEP height attribution in the shadow row, silent dropping of unrecognised Planning Portal layer groups (missed the Sydney Drinking Water Catchment constraint at Bowral), a false claim that the NSW state layer lacks data for an LGA when the gap is in our own ingest, blanket false s10.7(2) non-disclosure claims, and a Codes SEPP setback wrongly attributed to TI SEPP s2.120 — plus golden-sentence tests and a fail-soft lint extension so the defect class cannot silently return.

pre_impl.existing_data: Investigation was completed beforehand in the remediation plan (ce-conveyancing-integrity-remediation-2026-07): every claim in the Bowral PDF was verified against live NSW sources on 2026-07-06, including portal layerintersect for propId 1119594, the state HOB layer returning zero features, RFS BFPL returning zero features at the lot but one feature elsewhere in the LGA, and Valuer General values. Honest shadow-provenance wording already existed in the Intelligence Brief frontend and ShadowTool but was never ported to the PDF renderer.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The PDF assumed every shadow height was an LEP control when three of four height_source values are not; it assumed absence of a layerintersect group meant absence of the constraint when the portal simply is not exhaustive per LGA; and it assumed our spatial_overlays coverage table spoke for the NSW state layer. The prod ops check also disproved the suspected missing bushfire ingest: the statewide ALL coverage row exists with 223,847 features, so the Bowral footnote fired because LGA derivation returned nothing at that point, which the live RFS query now bypasses entirely.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new data sources were built: the live bushfire check reuses the existing production client _query_rfs_bfpl from services/bushfire_prescreen.py as a third parallel future, the honest shadow wording mirrors the existing Intelligence Brief copy, and the lint extension adds targets and one rule to the existing lint_brief_failsoft.py rather than forking a new linter. New code is confined to pure sentence-builder functions extracted so the exact user-visible wording is testable without reportlab.
pre_impl.external_source_error: If the RFS BFPL ArcGIS service times out, errors, or returns an error body, _query_rfs_bfpl returns is_bushfire_prone None and build_bushfire_row renders 'Not assessed — RFS service unavailable', falling back to the ingested PostGIS hit only when one exists — a failed live query can never render as 'Clear'. If the shadow pipeline is unreachable the row stays 'Not assessed', and if the portal layerintersect returns unrecognised groups they are captured verbatim and logged at WARNING instead of being dropped.
pre_impl.frontend_type: The free-tier JSON contract gains optional keys only (sdwc, other_instruments, and class/map_title inside sepp_overlays entries), so the existing ConveyancingTool display and cached conveyancing_cache blobs from older code read cleanly with .get() defaults; confidence remains one of the same three string values, now computed with integrity caps. No TypeScript changes were needed and jest was not touched.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before this change a conveyancer reading the Bowral PDF saw a fabricated '9 m LEP maximum height' claim, a missing drinking-water-catchment constraint with a cover tile saying CONSTRAINTS: None, a false statement that bushfire was not mapped for the LGA, and 'Confidence: high' — all silently wrong in a document meant for legal due diligence. Failure now surfaces visibly: assumed heights are labelled as assumptions, failed queries render 'Not assessed', unknown portal layers print under Other planning instruments, and confidence caps at medium when coverage or provenance is degraded.

functions.name: build_shadow_row
functions.input: the shadow pipeline outputs dict with height_m, height_source, adg_compliant and Jun 21 scenarios, or None when the pipeline was unreachable
functions.output: a (text, style_key, source_label) tuple where LEP attribution and the 'NSW LEP' source label appear only for height_source values that trace to an LEP control
functions.if_none: None renders 'Not assessed'; height_source 'default' renders the assumed-envelope wording and never asserts Clear; a missing or unrecognised height_source fails closed to the assumed-envelope label rather than claiming the LEP

functions.name: build_bushfire_row
functions.input: the live RFS BFPL result dict (or None on failure) plus the ingested PostGIS bushfire hit dict when one exists
functions.output: a (text, style_key, source_label) tuple: alert with the RFS category when prone, Clear citing the live query when not prone, alert from ingested data or Not-assessed when the live query failed
functions.if_none: both inputs missing yields 'Not assessed — RFS service unavailable' with the note style, so a network failure can never be rendered as a Clear verdict

functions.name: build_unmapped_note
functions.input: the covered_layers set (or list from cache, or None when coverage could not be determined)
functions.output: the coverage footnote owning the gap as PlotDetect's ingested data, or None when everything is covered; bushfire is deliberately excluded because it is live-checked
functions.if_none: None coverage returns no footnote at all rather than fabricating a claim about which layers are or are not mapped

functions.name: parse_controls
functions.input: the raw layerintersect response list from the NSW Planning Portal for a property
functions.output: the controls dict, now including a verbatim sdwc entry for the drinking water catchment and an other_instruments list capturing every unrecognised layer group with its titles
functions.if_none: an unrecognised group is appended to other_instruments and logged at WARNING instead of silently discarded; empty results blocks are still skipped so no phantom entries appear

functions.name: _compute_confidence
functions.input: controls, overlays and valuation as before, plus optional covered_layers, shadow_height_source and live_query_failures integrity signals
functions.output: high, medium or low where field completeness builds the base score and integrity gaps cap it — unmapped coverage layers or a defaulted shadow height cap at medium, two or more live failures cap at low
functions.if_none: callers that pass no integrity signals get the old completeness behaviour unchanged, so the free-tier endpoint keeps working while gaining the coverage cap it now passes

values.read_at: shadow_detector._get_height_limit fallback; surfaces in the PDF only through build_shadow_row's assumed-envelope wording, never as an LEP claim
values.if_missing: if height_source is absent from the outputs dict the row fails closed to the assumed-envelope label — provenance is never inferred

values.read_at: build_shadow_row when deciding whether LEP attribution is permitted for the shadow row
values.if_missing: any value outside the set (including default, None, or a future unrecognised source) renders assumed-envelope wording, so new sources must opt in explicitly

values.read_at: pre-commit hook runs the lint with default targets, which now include generate_conveyancing_report.py and services/conveyancing.py
values.if_missing: removing a file from the target list silently drops its except-block coverage — the lint's scope is visible in its pre-commit output on every run

queries: N/A — no DB queries were added or modified; the only database interaction in this change was a read-only pre-implementation ops check of spatial_overlays_coverage (bushfire ALL row present, 223,847 features), and the existing get_unique_overlays SQL is untouched.

break_it.scenario: A cached conveyancing_cache blob written by the previous deploy lacks the new sdwc and other_instruments keys when the PDF endpoint unpacks it
break_it.what_happens: generate_pdf reads both via controls.get() with None/empty defaults, so the report renders without the SDWC row exactly as the old parser would have produced
break_it.mitigated: yes — every new controls key is read defensively so stale cache blobs render cleanly
break_it.how: all new keys are read with .get() and or-[] guards; no code path indexes controls['sdwc'] without a truthiness check first
break_it.repro: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); from generate_conveyancing_report import parse_controls; c=parse_controls([]); c.pop('sdwc'); c.pop('other_instruments'); print(c.get('sdwc'), c.get('other_instruments') or [])"

break_it.scenario: The RFS BFPL service is down while the property genuinely is bushfire prone and our PostGIS ingest has the polygon
break_it.what_happens: the live query returns None, build_bushfire_row falls back to the ingested hit and renders an alert row labelled as ingested data with the live check noted unavailable — the buyer still sees the constraint
break_it.mitigated: yes — three-state row semantics keep the ingested alert visible whenever the live check fails
break_it.how: explicit three-state semantics in build_bushfire_row: live result governs, ingested hit is the failure fallback, and 'Clear' is only reachable from a successful live query

break_it.scenario: The live RFS query says not prone but the stale PostGIS ingest still contains a bushfire polygon for the lot
break_it.what_happens: the reconciliation block at the top of generate_pdf strips the stale overlay and logs a warning, so the cover tile, risk row, Section 5 note and consultant table all agree with the live answer instead of contradicting each other
break_it.mitigated: yes — pre-render reconciliation makes every PDF section agree with the live RFS answer
break_it.how: bushfire reconciliation runs before any rendering; the risk row is built from build_bushfire_row rather than the coverage-based flag() helper
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_conveyancing_truth.py::TestBushfireRowSemantics::test_live_clear_cites_live_rfs -q then inspect generate_pdf's _bf_live_prone branch

break_it.scenario: A future Planning Portal release adds a brand-new layerintersect group name this parser has never seen
break_it.what_happens: the group is captured verbatim into other_instruments, logged at WARNING so it surfaces in Railway logs, and rendered under Other planning instruments — deleting the else branch makes the zombie-layer test fail
break_it.mitigated: yes — the fail-open else branch plus a mutation test guarantee unknown groups surface
break_it.how: fail-open else branch in parse_controls plus the golden mutation test asserting the captured layer and titles

break_it.scenario: A Wingecarribee-profile report (unmapped coverage layers, defaulted shadow height) is served from the free-tier endpoint that previously claimed Confidence: high
break_it.what_happens: _compute_confidence caps the rating at medium from the covered_layers gap alone, and would cap at low if two live queries had also failed
break_it.mitigated: yes — integrity caps override the completeness score whenever coverage or provenance is degraded
break_it.how: integrity caps applied after the completeness score, exercised by five confidence tests including a clean-metro regression guard that must stay high

break_it.scenario: Someone reintroduces the blanket s10.7(2) claim or the TI SEPP 9 m setback wording in a future copy edit
break_it.what_happens: the static-claims guard scans the generator source for the forbidden phrases and fails the suite, and the reworded rows carry source_ref comments naming the actual instruments
break_it.mitigated: yes — a source-scanning guard test fails the suite if any forbidden claim returns
break_it.how: TestStaticClaimsGuard forbids six phrases including the fixed shadow source label, the state-layer blame sentence, and both false regulatory claims
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_conveyancing_truth.py::TestStaticClaimsGuard -q after re-adding any forbidden phrase to scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py

break_it.scenario: The nearby-DA fetch throws (DB down or ePlanning outage) during CLI or service PDF generation
break_it.what_happens: das becomes None instead of an empty list, and the DA section renders 'Not assessed — DA records could not be retrieved' instead of the previous confident 'No development applications lodged' claim
break_it.mitigated: yes — the extended lint blocks benign except-block fallbacks and das is now three-state
break_it.how: the new except-block lint rule flagged this exact fallback during development; das now uses three-state semantics (list, empty list, None) through both entry points
break_it.repro: python scripts/lint_brief_failsoft.py after reverting the das = None change — the lint fails on the benign except-block fallback
